real_estate.homebuilder: Pending home sales hit a record low nationally; here, homes in contract are down 29% from a year ago.
real_estate.commentary:
Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average is 7.45% this morning, down 0.01 from Wednesday, with the 15-year at 6.99%. Freddie Mac's weekly survey, out this morning, rose to 7.28% from 7.11%, its first increase since October 8 (the newsletter's 7.35% does not match Freddie's release). On today's $1,258,995 Fremont median with 20% down, that is about $7,008 a month in principal and interest.

Pending home sales fell 4.7% in October and 16.7% from a year ago, NAR reported, a second straight month at a record low. The West fell hardest, down 20.3% on the year. NAR's Lawrence Yun said October "could mark the low point in contract signings for this housing cycle."

Our own count points the same way, and more sharply (chart). On this date a year ago, 803 homes were in contract across the 14 cities in both of our exports; today it is 570, down 29%, while homes for sale rose 3% to 1,755. That is 3.1 homes for sale for every one in contract, up from 2.1. Fremont's contracts fell from 89 to 56, Hayward's from 97 to 59 and Newark's from 35 to 24.

Thursday's export shows 2,313 board wide, from 2,350 Wednesday, with 131 coming soon and 105 brand new. The five city ledger is 589, from 594: Fremont (197) fell three, Hayward (170) two and Milpitas (94) one, while Newark (72) added one and Union City (56) held.

What this means for you: buyers, with three homes on the market for every signed contract, you have time to compare and room to negotiate. Sellers, fewer buyers are signing, so price to today's comps rather than last spring's.

• Board wide: 2,313 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 131 coming soon and 105 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 589 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 524 are on the market and 65 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 197 live, 165 active, 23 coming soon and 9 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,258,995 at $778 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 41 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 170, Milpitas 94, Newark 72, Union City 56.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,036,500 at $666 a square foot. 258 homes are priced under a million, and 187 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

stocks.news:
Wednesday's close: the S&P 500 fell 0.23% and the Dow 1.11%, while the Nasdaq rose 0.42%. At 10:55 AM PT Thursday all three were lower: the S&P down 1.46%, the Dow down 1.70% and the Nasdaq down 1.56%.

San Francisco's Anthropic, the company behind Claude, priced its IPO Wednesday: 980 million shares at $83, raising $81.34 billion, the largest IPO ever, ahead of SpaceX's $75.0 billion in June (chart). Last week's filing called for 825 million shares at $70 to $78. Underwriters can buy 147 million more, and in a separate $26.0 billion private placement at the same price, Google and NVIDIA are each buying $10 billion. The stock opened Thursday at $111.50 under the ticker ANT, 34% above the offer price, and was at $95.13 (+14.61%) at 10:55 AM PT. A 34% pop at the open, and more than half of it gone by lunch.

feature_image.alt: Bar chart of the largest IPOs by base deal size in U.S. dollars: Anthropic, priced Nov. 18, 2026, $81.3 billion (980 million shares at $83, above the $64.4 billion top of the range it filed Nov. 10); SpaceX, June 2026, $75.0 billion; Saudi Aramco, December 2019, $25.6 billion; Alibaba, September 2014, $21.8 billion.
feature_image.caption: Anthropic's $81.34 billion raise is the largest IPO on record.
feature_image.source: SEC filings (Anthropic, SpaceX, Alibaba); Saudi Aramco

economy.note: Cards are Wednesday's settlements: the 10-Year from Treasury, gold and silver December COMEX futures, Brent ICE front month (January). Thursday's moves are in the text.
economy.commentary:
Minutes of the Fed's October 27 to 28 meeting, released Wednesday, show almost all officials judged that further rate increases would likely be appropriate, and many viewed the AI buildout as a material source of inflation risk. The committee held at 3.75% to 4% by a 10 to 2 vote, with two members preferring a quarter point hike, and a number of officials described housing as weak. The next decision is December 9. Not the holiday note mortgage shoppers were hoping for.

The 10-Year Treasury closed Wednesday at 5.07%, down 0.03. Gold settled Wednesday at $3,741.90, down 3.16%, and silver at $45.06, down 4.85%. Brent settled at $91.95, down 1.28%. The newsletter's 10-Year (5.05%), gold ($3,704, down 1.01%) and Brent ($91.80, down 0.16%) were evening quotes taken after Wednesday's close, and it left silver out. This morning gold is down 1.61% near $3,681.60, silver down 1.55% near $44.36, and Brent up 0.39% near $92.31.

crypto.commentary: Bitcoin is near $62,864, down 0.40% over the past 24 hours, live from CoinGecko at 10:55 AM PT. Ether is near $1,778.94 (+0.58%) and XRP near $0.97 (-0.59%). Crypto sat still while the IPO took the spotlight.
